# daymath

> ISO 8601 calendar day math for JavaScript. date-fns-shaped function names. Temporal.PlainDate under the hood. No silent local now. A Date or a time zone enters through day() and nowhere else.

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/daymath
- Source: https://github.com/leemr/daymath
- Playground: https://leemr.github.io/daymath/
- Changelog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- Contributing: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Future / backlog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/FUTURE.md
- Types: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.d.ts
- Implementation: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.js

## Install

```bash
npm install daymath
```

```js
import { day, addDays, differenceInDays, isSameDay } from 'daymath'
```

## Contract

- Inputs: ISO day string `YYYY-MM-DD` or expanded `±YYYYYY-MM-DD`, or Temporal.PlainDate from any implementation
- Range: `-271821-04-19` … `+275760-09-13` (Temporal PlainDate limit); outside it throws RangeError
- Outputs: ISO day strings (Temporal toString form)
- Date objects: TypeError on every public path including isValid(Date), except day()
- day(moment?, tz?): the calendar day of a moment, in a zone. Defaults are stated: moment is now, zone is 'utc'. moment accepts Date, epoch MILLISECONDS (as new Date(n) reads it), ISO day string, PlainDate, or an ISO timestamp carrying Z or an offset. A day carries no time so a zone does not apply to it. A string carrying a [Zone] annotation names its own zone, keeps its own civil day, and ignores the UTC default; passing tz as well throws. '11/12/2026' and '2026-08-08T12:00' (no offset and no zone, so daymath would have to pick) are refused; '2026-08-08T12:00[America/New_York]' is accepted. A lone string takes one of four roles in this order: day, zoned time, instant, then zone; the zone test is by shape (an IANA name, which carries no colon, or a bare offset like +05:30). A calendar annotation is ACCEPTED exactly where the other exports accept it, and day() then DROPS it, because day() is the normaliser: all three input shapes answer a plain ISO day, so day('2026-08-08T12:00[America/New_York][u-ca=buddhist]'), day('2026-08-08T20:00:00Z[u-ca=buddhist]') and day('2026-08-08[u-ca=buddhist]') all answer '2026-08-08'. A calendar that renumbers months or days is refused where it is APPLIED, which means with a zone bracket and on a day string; without a bracket the string names an Instant, which has no fields for a calendar to renumber, so the annotation is inert. Only export that reads a clock; only door a Date enters by. Never returns a Date, never stores the zone.
- Calendars: a `[u-ca=…]` annotation is ACCEPTED when the calendar only relabels the year, and REFUSED when it renumbers months or days. The line is measured at runtime, never held as a list, so a calendar CLDR adds later needs no code change: the month and day must equal the ISO fields and the year offset must be constant, checked on nine probe dates from 1900 to 2100 with two pairs straddling a Japanese era boundary. Today that accepts buddhist (+543), roc (−1911), japanese (0) and gregory (0), and refuses the other eleven it can build. The annotation rides along, so getYear('2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]') is 2569 and addDays gives '2026-02-01[u-ca=buddhist]'. iso8601 is accepted and dropped rather than carried. The rule reads Temporal, not Intl: Intl reports the ERA year, Reiwa 8 and B.R.O.C. 12, where Temporal reports a continuous year. Needs temporal-polyfill/full, which costs 4.2 kB gzip, because the base polyfill can build only iso8601 and gregory. daymath selects `globalThis.Temporal ?? bundled` itself, because the /full entry is a bare re-export with no selection of its own; so native Temporal runs where it exists, and the bundled full polyfill elsewhere. Both build the same sixteen calendars.
- Mixed calendar pair: a day is the same day whatever its year is labelled, so measurement normalises both sides to ISO instead of throwing. differenceInDays('2026-03-01', '2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]') is 29, and isEqual('2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]', '2026-01-31') is true. Temporal's own since and until refuse this with `Mismatched calendars`. Only exports that read or write a field honour the label.
- A Temporal STRING's date part is always ISO, so '2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]' is the same day as '2026-01-31'. The FIELDS form is different: from({year:2026, calendar:'buddhist'}) is ISO 1483-01-31, 543 years away. daymath takes strings and PlainDate objects, never the fields form, so it inherits Temporal's rule. There is NO string spelling that puts the calendar's year in the date part; the annotation is the only carrier. '2569-08-08[u-ca=buddhist]' is valid and its getYear is 3112, because the date part is ISO 2569 and the annotation adds 543 on top.
- day() is the NORMALISER and is the one export that drops the annotation: it accepts every annotation the others accept, and returns a plain ISO day for all three input shapes — an instant, a zoned string, and a day. parse validates and preserves; day normalises. Every other export carries the annotation.
- DO NOT pass a non-ISO calendar's own year as a bare ISO year. It is the one way to get a wrong answer with no error. Buddhist 2567 is ISO 2024, a leap year, but 2567 read as ISO is not, because 543 mod 4 is 3. So isLeapYear('2567-01-01') is false, getDaysInMonth for February is 28, parse('2567-02-29') throws, and addDays('2567-02-28', 1) answers '2567-03-01'. The two rules disagree in 49 of the 101 Buddhist years from 2500 to 2600. February is the only month affected, because it is the only one whose length varies.
- A JS Date has NO calendar component. It is one number of milliseconds, and getUTCFullYear() is always Gregorian, so a Thai user's Date already holds 2026. The 2569 exists only at display time, via Intl with u-ca-buddhist. Recipe: day(theDate) for a plain ISO day; annotate it '[u-ca=buddhist]' to work in Buddhist years; Temporal.PlainDate.from({year: 2569, month: 8, day: 8, calendar: 'buddhist'}) to convert FROM a Buddhist year number; Intl for display.
- isValid(badString): false
- getMonth/setMonth: 1–12 ISO (1=January), NOT date-fns 0-based; getDay: 1=Monday…7=Sunday ISO, NOT date-fns 0=Sunday; weekStartsOn default 7, 0 also accepted for Sunday
- differenceInMonths counts a month as full when addMonths would carry the earlier date to the later one, so 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-28 is 1; differenceInMonths(addMonths(d,n),d) === n always holds
- isSameDay is an alias of isEqual
- format only supports pattern yyyy-MM-dd (identity normalize); not locale display
- Intervals: { start, end }; areIntervalsOverlapping defaults inclusive false like date-fns

## When to use

- Pure calendar storage and math (hire date, trip day, passport day as strings)
- Swapping date-fns *names* while keeping string days (not a drop-in for Date-based code)

## When not to use

- Display formats like "MMM d" — use Temporal toLocaleString or date-fns
- Zoned times or instant math — use Temporal Instant/ZonedDateTime; day() converts an instant to a day but keeps no time

## PRs

Fork and open a pull request. Do not expect direct push access. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep 100% coverage on index.js.
